text_fidelity_a:
Everlast Reflex Bag (EA) [[VIDEOID:36c82b800aaf42202e179eeb3c1739a5]] I got this bag for my 9 year old son because he has some coordination issues. I wanted him to work eye hand coordination and get some exercise. He really enjoys working out with this reflex bag.

We filled our base with a 50 lb bag of sand rather than water. I figured that it would end up in the house and I didn't like the idea a flood on wood floors if it leaked. Also that quanity of sand is twice as heavy as the same amount of water. This means the bag will stay upright if it gets hit hard. The play sand that we used had to be dried on a tarp to get it to pour into the opening. When it was damp it had to be forced into the opening and it took a long time to get a small quantity of sand inside. Other than that it was very easy to assemble. Everlast provides a hex key and a cheap stamped out wrench to assemble the bag.

It does unscrew slightly form the base as it is struck. This should not be a deal breaker for you, but something you need to be aware of.

Other reviewers have posted negative reviews must be hitting this bag with powerful blows. From my experience a reflex bag is more for speed and reflex training than power blows. If you want to lay into something with power, get a heavy bag. It will suit you much better.

For our use we are very happy with the bag. I think any kid would really enjoy this as a gift. Dad likes it too, and I like that my son getting some exercise rather than sitting in his room playing with his Nintendo DSi.

We got the Everlast 8 ounce Youth gloves to go with this Reflex Bag. I would recommend them as they offer good wrist support and excellent construction.

[[ASIN:B000QSQKDW Everlast Pro Style 8-Ounce Youth Training Gloves]]

Update5/26/10: Yesterday one on my son's friend used a bat on the reflex bag. It is not bat proof. It knocked the bag off. I poured Gorilla glue into the hole and on the post and let it dry with the post pointed up for a day. It seems as good as new.

Update 7/3/10 The bag is better than new. Two kids parties and near daily use and the bag is still firmly on the pole. The Gorilla glue has secured this bag with no sign of wiggle. They should manufactur them like this.

Update 11/8/11 The bag is still on as good as when I first glued it. No wiggle. The unit has been stored on our patio and is starting to rust at the spring and shaft. Nothing that affects the performance. It's just not that sightly. My son wants a B.O.B. Body Opponent Bag It is a training bag that looks like a torso. $250...ouch.
text_fidelity_b: Everlast Reflex Bag (EA)

text_fidelity_a:
Kelty Salida Camping and Backpacking Tent, 2 Person Solid tent, but I ultimately ended up selling it.

The good: was waterproof, quick to set up, didn't get any condensation on the trips that I used it, reasonably lightweight for the price, came with quality lightweight stakes. Plenty of room for 1 person to sprawl out, sit up, etc.

The so-so: I didn't like the square pack, packed to 14" H x 13" W x 4" D. Fit in an 11L compression sack (excluding stakes and poles), and compressed nicely in that regard. It has only one door, so if you're sharing, you're climbing over one another. Too small for 2 people unless you like sleeping on top of one another.

Why did I sell it? It was too big in my pack for a 1P tent, but its floor space is too small for 2P. For 1 person, it would be a decent car camping option, or backpacking if you're a larger person.

I'm debating the Salida 1 as its replacement, so it isn't a knock against the tent, just the size didn't work for me.
text_fidelity_b: Kelty Salida Camping and Backpacking Tent, 2 Person

2 Pack Camping Lanterns Camping Accessories USB Rechargeable and Battery Powered 2-in-1 LED Lanterns, Hurricane Lights with Flashlight and Magnet Base for Camping, Hurricane, Hiking, Emergency, Outage What doesn’t it do?

That was my son’s reaction when I first showed off this light to him. We had similar one from a popular manufacturer that recently broke. We used it all the time for camping and during power outages. This one does everything that lantern did and more.

I was skeptical about the brightness of the flashlight feature. It appears to be a fairly large COB with a projection (magnifying) lens over it. I used it in my backyard tonight and it’s just about as bright as a standard LED flashlight.
The strobes are a cool feature. I hope to never use them in an emergency but have some fun playing with them with my kids. The magnetic base is cool too. Good for use under a car hood or under the vehicle itself. Strong enough magnets to keep it in its place.

The lantern is why I bought this. It’s bright, lightweight, and somewhat durable. It lights up a tent or cabin real nice. We use them during power outages as well (we get a handful a year). The battery life Is to be determined. I haven’t had this one long enough to go through the internal battery and I haven’t put AA’s in it yet. I’m not sure I will. I love the fact this is rechargeable and even though we all have the cables, this came with 2 of them. Nice touch.
It would be nice to see the handles coated (rubberized or similar). I’ve seen some nice lanterns that have that, but at double or more the cost of these.

This Hauler has proven itself both versatile and durable. Since I first purchased it, I have used it for a multitude of tasks and have only replaced one tire and four tubes in that 20 year period. It has taken about as much punishment as any tool I own. Like Timex watches "it takes a licking and keeps on ticking".

I have used this Sunlite Standard Schrader Valve Tube as a replacement tube for the ones I've damaged during hard use. Originally I went to a local bicycle shop and paid around $19.95 per tube but took a look on Amazon and found the same product for only $7.95. That is close to being three tubes for the price of one (locally) and it is delivered free to my home.

Having it delivered to me saves about an hour of my time that I would have spend driving to/from and waiting for a salesperson to pull the tube. Time gets more valuable as I get older so I appreciate any time that I can use to be more productive. I always make sure that I have a spare tube sitting on the shelf for the next repair in case one gets punctured. Of course that seems to always happen at the worst possible time so it's nice to have a new one available.
text_fidelity_b: Sunlite Standard Schrader Valve Tube

The bag itself is very sturdy, made from authentic Real Tree camouflage fabric. There are 14 very well padded golf club compartments. The well padded shoulder strap is removable with large hooks, and which beneath this large strap are smaller elastic lift handles. There is also a very sturdy cupped lift handle on the opposite side, making for easy lifting.

The bag has a total of 13 pockets- two of which are mesh and the other 11 are zippered. Besides the 2 small net pockets, there are 2 very large zipper pockets for clothing or large items. There are also large, medium and small zippered pockets for various items like your balls or tees. There is a small lined pocket for your valuables as well as a Cooler pocket which is very well padded and vented for condensation.

Besides all these great pockets, there is a loop and tie to hold an umbrella, as well as a hook to hold a towel and even a rubber edged hole to hold a pen or pencil. To keep everything in your bag under cover, they've included a great cover you can snap onto the golf bag. Amazingly, even with so many compartments, pockets and being well-padded, this cart bag is surprisingly light weight. This 4 1/2 Star cart bag may be just a standard bag, but the pockets give it lot of great bells and whistles for keeping you organized on the course.

text_fidelity_a: Bushnell G-Force 1300 ARC Laser Rangefinder I was looking to purchase a new unit for sometime.  My previous unit was a Bushnell from the early 90's, and it delivered faithful service for almost 20 years.  It finally died, so I began to look for a good replacement.  This product has a backlit feature that really helps in either bright, or low light situations.  On large objects, (A surrounding hillside) I was able to get it to range out to 1200+ yards repeatedly.  The compact size and power of this unit is a major step up from my 1st generation unit.  I will have to see as to long term durability, but the case housing feels solid, and it has survived a few outings into the High Desert summer time extreme temperatures (115'+).  It comes with a fairly useful carrying case with a magnetic closure, and a rather complicated carrying strap I found to be useless.  The directions are straight forward, and the ACR (Angle Range Compensation) feature does work,  is not TOO complicated and has been useful in my target shooting.  I do not give this product 5 stars because I have not had it long enough to determine it's long term durability.
text_fidelity_b: Bushnell G-Force 1300 ARC Laser Rangefinder

Cutter 66384 Camping-Candles, pack of 1, silver If you take the time to research the product, regardless of who markets it, you will find that citronella, as a mosquito repellent, does not, will not, CAN NOT do what it is advertised to do.
The best mosquito repellent is a slight breeze. These insects have extreme difficulty flying/navigating in the slightest breeze.

The reason you see dead mosquitoes in the wax, flame (or light of most types) attracts them. When they fly into the flame, wings, antennaeI, and proboscis get burned off. They fall into the hot wax, and die.

I buy these, locally, to use while fishing. Buy only for the light provided.
To sum it up: people have been told, for decades, that citronella repels mosquitoes, they are persuaded that it works, not noticing a slight breeze, in stead it’s, “Oh, my word! This stuff works!!!”
Do some research. Read a bit. And save your money.
Type in your search engine: how citronella works.
Be amazed !!!

text_fidelity_a:
TRX Training Bandit Kit, Home-Workout Resistance-Band Set with Strength-Training Resistance Bands and Universal-Fit Handles for Exercise Bands UPDATE:
So it's been a bit since we've had this TRX Bandit Kit, Resistance-Band Set, including it in our workouts, coming away continuing to be disappointed. My original review is below, for which I originally gave the set a 3 star rating. We decided to drop it to 2 stars because 1. without the second band that was supposed to be included, but was not, our workout weights are completely limited to one level, and 2. even with the second set - which we would have still liked to have been included - this type of set is limited in the scope of the numbers/types of workouts one can do with it.

1. The set only came with one of two sets of bands promised on the product page and on the box. Without that second set you are limited to only 1 weight level, not the 3 it should have offered: one set, second set, combined set. In other words, it's kind of like, what's the point? Very limiting.

2. But even with the second set, this kind of resistance band offers few exercises. We recently got two other types of resistance band sets, the type with the bungie-like cords (2 sets in each for different weights - actually were included) and anchors and accessories (like a bar, door anchor, etc), that expand the ways you can use the bands. In fact, each of those sets offers at least a dozen (or more) ways to use the set. Then add in the various weight combinations and you have a far better set.

My wife and I really like the TRX brand, finding that other products in their line up work well and offer a range of options, but this TRX Bandit Kit, Resistance-Band Set is really not worth it. It's extremely limited, especially without half the set. Therefore, we cannot recommend it higher than a 2 star rating.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
My wife and I are big fans of the TRX product line, with a suspension training system as part of our workout lives. So when I had the chance to grab this TRX Bandit Kit, Resistance-Band Set for Home Gyms I jumped. In general, this set SHOULD earn a 5 star rating. However, while the box and product page clearly state there are TWO SETS OF BANDS INCLUDED - our only had ONE. Therefore, I cannot give this review more than 3 stars. This is a basic quality control issue and for a well known exercise brand, not having that second (BLUE) set in the box reflects badly on the brand. I have come to almost expect such disappointment from unknown brands, and even there, it doesn't happen as much as one would think. But that a major brand like TRX would have such a blatant issue is disappointing and frustrating.

The TRX Bandit Kit, Resistance-Band Set for Home Gyms itself seems as though it's going to work great for us. We already use resistance band sets in our workouts and adding this TRX version was and is going to be an easy move. We already like the handle set up. It's easy to get the band into the handle and the handle itself is well made and comfortable for both our hands to grip and keep control. In the 24 hour we have had it we have each used it once in testing, so no great workout yet, but the handles and green bands gave us each a nice burn. This will be a compliment to other equipment, and one that will also work when we travel, being small and easy to pack.

In the end we believe this TRX Bandit Kit, Resistance-Band Set for Home Gyms deserves 5 stars for giving us another layer of workout, but we cannot give it anything more than 3 stars due to the glaring issue of quality control when assembling the set. Missing the blue bands cuts the product in half as far as what one can do with it and at this (or any) price point, that's not acceptable, especially from such a well known company.
text_fidelity_b: TRX Training Bandit Kit, Home-Workout Resistance-Band Set with Strength-Training Resistance Bands and Universal-Fit Handles for Exercise Bands

text_fidelity_a:
TOPOKO 25 OZ Hydro Double Wall Flask Stainless Steel Water Bottle, Bite Valve Top, Vacuum Insulated, Sweat Proof, Leak Proof Sports Thermos. Standard Mouth 25oz, BPA-Free, Keep Cold 24 Hours (Orange) As someone who like cold drinks and who lives in a warm climate, I realized my plastic bottles weren't keeping me happy. I had two stainless steel bottles around the house but one was designed for hot coffee and therefore a bit on the small size for someone who wants to fill it with a cold drink and a few cubes of ice. The other bottle was really similar to this only it had a twist off top and the top part was too small to squeeze standard ice cubes in. Took a chance on this one. The mouth is perfect for fitting ice cubes in. I went with the "bite" lid because I kind of get tired of opening and closing the bottle constantly and the straw lid seemed to get mixed reviews. The bite lid, so far, is perfect. I use it all day every day for my water. I have found the bite lid works best if you don't fully extend it, more like pull it up half way. When closed I shook it around and it didn't leak but I probably still wouldn't keep it in say a bag with anything important in it. I was using a slightly larger plastic bottle but find this bottle in this size is great as I don't need to cram as much ice in the bottle to keep it chilled.

I have seen some reviews that say the color coating peels off, I haven't had that experience thus far but I have heard of other bigger brand name bottles having the same issue when coated like this one is, so it wouldn't surprise me. Will update when / if I experience it.
text_fidelity_b: TOPOKO 25 OZ Hydro Double Wall Flask Stainless Steel Water Bottle, Bite Valve Top, Vacuum Insulated, Sweat Proof, Leak Proof Sports Thermos. Standard Mouth 25oz, BPA-Free, Keep Cold 24 Hours (Orange)

Coleman Xtreme Cooler, Large Ice Box, PU Full Foam Insulation, Stays Cool for Days, Portable Cool Box; Perfect for Camping, Picnics and Festivals We keep one of these in the house at all times next to the kitchen to use as an extension to our refrigerator. We use it for both cold and hot food storage. For cold storage you can put a couple gallon jugs of frozen water in the cooler and it will keep the temperature between 37F and 39F for several days. We use the cooler to thaw meat, party prep, seasonal cooking prep, and anytime we run out of space in the refrigerator after a trip to the grocery store, big box store, etc. For hot storage we use it for resting hot smoked meats after they have been taken off the smoker. Cleanup and disinfection is a breeze.

We used three of these on a weeklong desert camping trip to an art and music festival, temps in the low to high 90s. These babies definitely keep ice for 5 days. We had one of them under our shade structure up off the playa surface with wooden blocks and the other two we kept up on wooden blocks in a covered cargo trailer. The one under our shade structure was opened and closed quite a bit because it contained our fresh food. The other two had alcoholic drinks and were opened less often because we were consuming mostly water. We bought ice on the 5th day but there was still quite a bit of ice present in the melt water. The ones in the trailer had lots of ice but they weren't opened as much. We drained the melt water to use for shower water and only charged them with ice one more time before we left the desert, and we did so just because it was relatively convenient and we wouldn't be unpacking them right away when we got home. Great coolers especially for the price.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Xtreme Cooler, Large Ice Box, PU Full Foam Insulation, Stays Cool for Days, Portable Cool Box; Perfect for Camping, Picnics and Festivals

Polar M400 GPS Smart Sports Watch I love my Polar M400. It does a great job of tracking my heart rate, it's easy to read, and I love all the features (I'm sure there are many I'm not even aware of yet). This device is incredibly customizable, and alerts, while not silent, are not obnoxious or loud either. It is a little large, but for a man, not so much that it looks bad. It's actually fairly attractive even just as a watch (though if you aren't going to use it as a fitness device, don't spend the money on it just for use as a watch).

As far as exercise tracking, I do find that I occasionally forget to start it recording, but that is my own fault and really not much different from any other trackers out there. I would like to see some other types of activities available, such as jumping rope (this is even an activity it recommends to reach your goal, so why not be able to record it?). I sometimes use my speed rope for warm-up and for cardio, and the only selection I can really make for recording this activity while using the heart rate monitor is "Other Indoor". I'd also love to see a way to move more easily from one exercise to another, rather than having to completely stop recording then go back in and select the next exercise. I know the V800 has such a feature, so I can't imagine it would take much more than a software update. Since the V800 has other features not available on the M400, I wouldn't think adding this to the M400 would detract from V800 sales. Those who want the additionally functionality offered by the V800 are likely looking beyond just quick changes between exercises. Either way, it's still not a deal breaker for me, nor is it difficult to transition.

I have not experienced the sync issues others have complained about. I did have trouble once, but it was of my own doing as to when I enabled bluetooth on my phone to start the sync.

I love the fitness test, because I like having an idea of my VO2 Max. If you do any kind of heart rate training, you're probably familiar with this concept, and it also gives a good "summary" view of your overall cardiovascular health. I believe this is also what allows the M400 to be able to fairly accurately determine your calorie burn whether during exercise or just regular daily activity.

As far as the heart rate monitoring, I have no reason to believe it is inaccurate in any way. I used to use a Sportline META 1075 which I loved! I loved having it act both as my MP3 player while I exercised, and I loved having it read out my heart rate to me audibly. That said, the Sportline only gave me time exercising, max heart rate, min heart rate, and average heart rate. The Polar provides SO much more information that, while I miss having my heart rate "announced" to me, I find the additional information from the Polar much more useful. I also love the graphs of my heart rate. This is something the Sportline could not provide, as it didn't record the information or allow for transfer to another device. Aside from resistance training (for which I also like knowing my heart rate), I do both heart rate-based and interval training. It's great to be able to see a graph of your heart rate as it peaks and recovers during intervals to see how your cardio vascular system is improving. It's also nice to see things like your running pace, average and max, and a graph of it, over the duration of your run. These are things I haven't had before, and it is interesting again to see not only how I am doing, but how I am progressing, as I can go back and compare current workouts to previous ones.

I've also had no problem with the water resistance. I haven't worn the device swimming, but I have forgotten to take it off while showering, and it hasn't had any issues.

I would definitely recommend this device for any fitness enthusiast!
text_fidelity_b: Polar M400 GPS Smart Sports Watch

text_fidelity_a: INVOKER Ultralight Inflatable Camping Sleeping Pad - Mat with Built-in Foot Pump, Lightweight Compact Air Mattress, Best Sleeping Pads for Backpacking Travel Hiking Beach, Fully Inflate in 25s I'm not a hiker, but I do have an SUV tent, an air mattress that fits the back of the SUV and now an air pillow.  I'm a bit different than most folks because I actually sleep on a 20" tall queen size air mattress every night and have done so for the past two years.  The thing is, with the air mattress I can move and sleep in may different positions and my body feels supported.  That's not exactly how or why I use a pillow.  Again, I'm not like most people - I have been sleeping with a 100% down pillow for so many years I can't even remember when I bought my first one.  I mention this because of the way I use a pillow when sleeping - it is molded, puffed out and reformed several times during the night.  That just can't happen with this air pillow.  For me, it serves more as a back prop for sitting up and reading on the bed.  Nice and firm, it gives me back support while sitting up in bed.  It does store well in the very small case it comes in and that's perfect!  As I have gotten older and had to move when I didn't really want to but circumstances made me, I have become addicted to "nomadic furniture" that is easier to move than traditional furniture.  An air pillow does fit within my parameters of small and packable!  Same with my bed - not quite a small, but certainly nothing like lugging around a heavy, floppy queen size mattress and box springs!  So, all in all, I am pleased with this air pillow at least for what I will use it for.
text_fidelity_b: INVOKER Ultralight Inflatable Camping Sleeping Pad - Mat with Built-in Foot Pump, Lightweight Compact Air Mattress, Best Sleeping Pads for Backpacking Travel Hiking Beach, Fully Inflate in 25s

text_fidelity_a: Thule Insta-Gater Truck Bed Bike Rack, Black, One Size After days of research (!) I decided to order this product.  I don't think I would have chosen this product it had been from a company other than Thule, Yakima, Saris, Hollywood etc... i.e. it needed to be backed by a company with market share as the concept is unique.  Installation was a breeze.  I was a bit worried when I first used it and found that my front tire sits up on the cross piece in a small "v" - but my concern went away after the first trip and I've not thought about it again after 15+ trips.  My bike is a Giant Hybrid (small frame).  The product shipped very quickly and the materials are quality.  Yes once you open the tail gate the bike does require you to use one hand to stabilize it, but thanks to other reviewers I was prepared and hopefully I'm preparing the next readers!  I am able to lock the bike to the rack and the rack to the truck and when I'm on the trail the rack folds down small enough I simply toss in the front floor board of the cab.  I've had to stop once and tighten it as I was traveling down a washed out "road" with deep ruts.  I looked in the rear view mirror and saw my front tire just beginning to move.  It could have been from the deep ruts or I simply didn't get the required "two clicks" tension.  Highway speeds have proven no issue.  I like the fact that my license plate and tail lights are not obstructed as with a more traditional rack and certainly nothing is sticking out beyond the width of my vehicle.  Some states the above issues can result in a ticket - no thanks!  The price point is excellent as is the product.  I would highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Insta-Gater Truck Bed Bike Rack, Black, One Size

Freetrack Men's Reflective Cycling Rain Jacket Waterproof Hooded Windbreaker Running/Hiking/Golf Jackets My wife and I live in a hot weather, humid state that has a rainy season - that has of course, since ordering this, has dropped off as we near the end of it. We’d been out for a few days, enjoying things, when we got caught out. We do go out with light rain ponchos, but they can get hot, sticky, and not cover very well. This last time was, well, the last time we wanted to use them. I had been looking for a rain jacket for both my wife and I and spotted this Freetrack Men's Reflective Cycling Rain Jacket Waterproof Hooded Windbreaker for myself. I am already thrilled with it and I haven’t even worn it in the rain. This Freetrack Men's Reflective Cycling Rain Jacket Waterproof Hooded Windbreaker looks great! I love the navy, the reflective line, and the layout of the pockets. I put it on and it was a perfect fit. The cut is good - I feel like I can wear just my t shirt or light color shirt and shorts and I’ll be covered well. But I’m also loosing weight, so I feel like as I do, it’ll get big, but still cover me well, perhaps even better.

There is great placement of velcro - at the wrists to hold it tight, along the front to keep it truly secure. The front zipper is covered so as to not let rain in the front. The hood comes up and over, with the ability to pull it down “tight” to protect the face/head. The material truly does feel like it’ll repel rain and keep me dry. I also have to think about keeping cool - in our hot, humid state rain can make things even more steamy - and this feels like it’ll be good. I’m not saying I’ll be “cool,” but rather comfortable in the rain.

I hope we have some rain in the coming days, as predicted, and as soon as we do, I’ll give it a good test. But until then, I’m already thrilled and happy to have this Freetrack Men's Reflective Cycling Rain Jacket Waterproof Hooded Windbreaker. I’ll update when I can, but until then, this Freetrack Men's Reflective Cycling Rain Jacket Waterproof Hooded Windbreaker was a good find!

Soddeph 1.3 Gallon Collapsible Water Container Bag, BPA Free Food Grade Clear Plastic Storage Jug for Sport Camping Riding Mountaineer,Freezable,Food Grade (1.3 Gal, 2-pack) As we live in a hurricane prone area we decided to add these to our preparedness collection. Along with our gallons of water we thought it would be a good idea to grab these. Unlike the gallon we’ll full these bags up last minute and use for cooking and cleaning water. They are very large and store a good amount of water, and with the their base that speaks out and sits well, it’ll be good to have around. But they don’t seem like they’ll be able to sit and hold water as we do for the entire 6 month season with our normal gallon jugs. No problem, again, we’ll fill them as a storm is approaching and use for short term storage.

The materials (plastic) seem like they’ll hold up. We have found with the gallon jugs there are quality differences: some are thin and will start to leak after a few months. We also do not keep them from season to season. As a season hits it’s end we’ll use that water for water and cooking and then restock for the next season. With these jugs we’ll fill as the storm approaches, then empty after it’s through and water is no longer needed.

I THINK I’ll be able to fill in the sink, but have not tried. It is large and we’d prefer doing a good cleaning on the sink before laying it inside. I did not take that time and instead filled it from the tub. That worked okay. I lost a good amount of water as the flow from that spigot is not great. But it filled in a few minutes and will sit fine.

Overall it’ll be a good back up and we’re happy to have them for our set up. Should we ever go camping (not something we do) or need water in a pinch, we’ll find other uses. But just the prep element is well worth having these around.
text_fidelity_b: Soddeph 1.3 Gallon Collapsible Water Container Bag, BPA Free Food Grade Clear Plastic Storage Jug for Sport Camping Riding Mountaineer,Freezable,Food Grade (1.3 Gal, 2-pack)

OMOTIYA Glow in The Dark Basketball, LED Light Up Basketball, Night Glowing Ball, Boys Girls Sports Gifts Accessories 8-12 Year Old, Toy Basketball Gifts Ideas for Age 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13+ Kid Teens If you look at the 4th and 5th pictures. . . as well as the video. . . you will see that this stripes are what illuminate. Not the entire ball. But this company offers an orange ball which does completely light-up, under a different listing.

This is a "light-up" ball, and not a "glow-in-the-dark" ball. The difference being that this one has lights inside and operates with batteries. A "glow-in-the-dark" ball is one where you place it in bright like for a bit. . .then it will "glow" for a few minutes. Because this is a "light-up" ball, the lights are brighter and will last longer. Also, there are additional batteries included, which is a plus.

There's not an "on/off" button. You simply bounce the ball and it will turn-on and illuminate. The lights will "turn-off" after a minute of not "agitation" / bounce.

This ball is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of forty bucks, I think it's a bit pricey. . . and it is more of a "toy". if you're looking for a "professional" basketball. . . this is not it. But it is a VERY cool ball to play with in the dark!

text_fidelity_a:
Callaway Men's Mack Daddy 2 Wedge (Slate Finish, Custom Sole C-Grind) Being a lifetime hacker (22 hcp), I was reluctant to spend a lot of money on a wedge, but I was in need of one desperately. My short game is usually my downfall so I researched and found the Callaway Mack Daddy 2. I chose to go with the 60 degree "C" grind due to the fact that I love to hit flop shots as well as standard chips, pitches, approaches, etc. Check out the videos on callaway's website for more info on which grind is best for you.

The wedge comes in a matte chrome or slate finish. I chose to go with the slate finish as I liked the darker look and thought I would like the oxidation look as well. Looking back I think I would likely have chosen the chrome finish as it requires less maintenance. The slate finish will rust and require you to scrub off the rust as time goes by. Callaway recommends you keep a small patch of Scotch-Brite Purple in your bag for scrubbing it off. A lubricant cleaner can also be used to help keep the rust off the finish.

The handling of this wedge is amazing. As I said, my short game has sucked, partly because I haven't put enough time in and partly because my wedge always was a hand-me-down. After getting this wedge and practicing with it quite a bit I'm in love. I usually use hard covered balls because I hate losing a nice soft covered ball. Even with using a hard covered ball I'm able to get some pretty good backspin on the ball when pitching or approaching the green. Flop shots are incredibly easy with this wedge thanks to the "C" grind and I've improved nearly every aspect of my short game in part to this club.

The groves are the highest degree allowed by the USGA and the laser etched pattern really helps put extra spin on the ball.

Overall I love this club immensely. It gives you great control of the ball with whatever shot you are trying to hit. I'm planning on picking up a 52 or 54 degree wedge as well, in the future. Excellent club, can't recommend it enough!
text_fidelity_b: Callaway Men's Mack Daddy 2 Wedge (Slate Finish, Custom Sole C-Grind)

text_fidelity_a:
OBOVA Bike Handlebar Bag 4L, Waterproof & Phone Holder, 4-Layer Bike Pouch For Handlebars, Bicycle Front Bag, Bicycle Bag Front Handlebar, Road, Mountain I've got a folding electric bike that I love, but I'm limited in the kinds of bags I can attach because a) the battery pack is mounted on the front and b) I have to think about how the bag might limit my ability to fold the bike (or how my need to fold the bike limits the kind bag I can mount). I wanted to buy a handlebar bag made by the company that makes my bike, but like so many items during the pandemic it was impossible to get. With some reluctance, I settled on this. Now I'm really happy that the company bag -- which was twice the price of this one -- was out of stock.

The velcro straps are strong and keep the bag in place even when I let the handlebars drop to fold away. Unlike some reviewers on here, the zippers have held up well for me so far, though the ones for the main compartment are still a bit stiff. I can use my phone easily through the transparent touch screen holder on the top, but getting it in and out of that pouch at first was extremely difficult. This has improved greatly over time, though. While my phone does fit even inside it's bulky case, it goes in much easier without the case on -- no surprise there, but it made me a little nervous at first. However, if I have my phone there on a ride, I leave it there and don't remove it until I get home and can return it to the case.

Since getting it, I've been caught in a couple of light rains and one heavier shower while riding with this bag. In all cases, everything inside the bag and it's various pouches remained bone dry. It does come with a rain cover, but that popped over my battery.

The only thing I don't like about the bag is that the stitching on the velcro patches on long exterior pouch (the one with the reflective stripe) aren't very well done. I don't use that pouch much, and I'm careful to slowly peel it open when I do, but I expect those to come off sooner rather than later. It was a bit disappointing to see the low quality work there when the rest of it is so well made, but there's more than enough space for me in the rest of the bag.

If I ever need to replace this bag, I'd definitely consider buying another one of these. The only thing I'd like to see changed (besides improving the stitching on that one pouch, that is) is to perhaps make the interior of the main compartment a contrast color rather than black like the exterior. Maybe that would increase the price a bit -- I'm sure it's cheaper to make everything the same color -- but I sometimes use the bag in low light conditions, and it can be a bit hard to find things. But even with the black interior, it's a good bag as it is and offers good quality at far better prices than many major brands.
text_fidelity_b: OBOVA Bike Handlebar Bag 4L, Waterproof & Phone Holder, 4-Layer Bike Pouch For Handlebars, Bicycle Front Bag, Bicycle Bag Front Handlebar, Road, Mountain

text_fidelity_a: SUNLITE Unicycle Cotterless Steel Crank Arm Set, Silver The first unicycle I had was in Germany when I was with the US Army in Heidelberg. It was a VERY hard to ride 26 or 28 inch. Not a good one to learn on. Changing it to a 24 inch by rebuilding the wheel (but keeping the same long cranks) made it much easier to ride. That was in 1983 and that unicycle has since worn out. (I rode it a LOT, all over the World!) But newer unicycles lacked the same quality of that ride and the "feel" was all wrong. I didn't even know that cranks came in different lengths in 1983, but reducing the large wheel diameter while keeping the 6 inch cranks is what made the ride so nice. (With shorter cranks it's not as easy to balance or pedal, and you go too fast- not impossible but not as much fun.) Proof of that came with these 6 inch SUNLITE cotterless cranks which changed the performance of a 24 inch that came with 5 inch cranks to finding that "sweet spot" it had been missing. They're very heavy and strong, I doubt I'll be able to bend these.
text_fidelity_b: SUNLITE Unicycle Cotterless Steel Crank Arm Set, Silver

The box included 4 CR123a batteries. You only need 2 for powering the light. Putting the batteries in place takes some talent by aligning the cover back to the base while the batteries are pressing against it. It is just a bit tricky but the cover will snap in place while holding with one hand and you can snap the lock with the other hand. The on/off switch in my opinion is in a good location. I also like that it stays out of the way from your finger until you need it.

Also the flashlight comes with additional clips for mounting it on a Picatinnny rail. The use of the clips will depend on what kind of hunting item you will be using it on. The stock one that came installed worked for me. They are easy to change out by removing a screw on the flashlight side. The included clips may also allow for how close you want the on /off switch to your finger.

Final thoughts: I like this brand and model. I also feel it is in a fair price range. The light is bright and should last a long time before having to replace the batteries. One more note is that to replace batteries, the flashlight will need to be taken off the Picatinny rail. I am giving this Feyachi flashlight 5 stars for good quality construction, value and brightness.

SainSmart Jr. Kids Bow and Arrows 2 Sets, Light Up Archery Set with 6 Suction Cups Arrows, Outdoor Hunting Game for 8-12 Toddlers I bought this bow and arrow set for my 3-year-old granddaughter. It is recommended for ages 4-8, so she’s a little young, and indeed it took her a bit of practice to master loading, drawing, and releasing an arrow. It’s been great training for both fine and gross motor skills.

The bow doesn’t have flexible limbs to power the arrows, like a traditional bow. Instead, it has rigid limbs and an elastic string that really does send the suction cup arrows sailing. Our favorite thing is shooting it at the sliding glass patio door. When the arrows fly true, they stick to the glass with a satisfying “splat”. We also like to shoot the stuffed chairs and sofa in the living room. We’ll shoot our bows outside once it warms up and some of the snow melts.

The bow has built-in LED lights that come on and start flashing when you grip the handle. That was an immediate hit with our toddler, and drew her to the bow right away. We mostly ignore that now. I don’t know how long the batteries will last but I expect that by the time they die, she will be more interested in sending arrows across the room than watching the flashing lights. Who knows - maybe this will be the start of a longer term interest in real archery.

Let me know if you found anything in my review helpful.

text_fidelity_a:
Infinite Discs Slinger Deluxe Bag I recently started playing disc golf again after about 20 years off. Right now I only throw 5 molds and 3 drivers, a mid and a putter. I have the putter in two different plastics, all others I just have one disc of, so I need to carry a total of 6 discs.

I do anticipate cycling the drivers and mids in base plastic, so I foresee me carrying 10-12 discs eventually, but this bag will still handle that. Right now, as a 46-year-old dad, I play with my 4-year-old and 9-year-old boys. This means I carry the 4-year-old's discs and a small jacket for him. I also actually carry a full-size bath towel right now because...boys and water hazards. And there's still plenty of room in this bag.

The putter pocket carries my driving/approach putter and my soft putting putter, the 3 slots inside carry my main three discs that I throw besides the putter, and there's room for all the other discs and kid gear that I carry.

The bag is comfortable to wear, the strap can be moved to the bottom right or bottom left side depending on how you want to carry it. When carried over my right shoulder and across my chest, the bag sits at a slight angle on your back. This is nice because it means you can leave the main compartment slightly unzipped to access your discs and not worry about them falling out as the zipper ends up being at an angle up from the ground. It stands up fine on the ground when it's full of discs and equipment, and it's pretty easy to get the discs in and out of, which was my only concern when I bought it.

As other reviews mention, it won't fit a huge 32 oz Nalgene water bottle, but I kind of plan on carrying something else in the drink compartment anyway. I could get my Klean Canteen in there and I would imagine there are others that fit just fine. Titan Fitness HD Multi-Grip Wall Mounted Pull-Up Bar, 48" Wide Grip, Rated 600 LB, Strength Accessory I'll come back to post pics. yes hardware to install would be nice, but people install to diff. surfaces and would need diff. hardware.

I used 2 2x6 boards to mount to studs. I would recommend using 2x8 if I did it again. I anchored them with 8 - 5" lag bolts at the outer edges and 12 - 4" structural screws at the middle studs.

for anyone having problems getting the lags in that are on the upper side of the bottom bracket. mount the top section of the pull bar first. drill your pilot holes in the correct location for the bottom brackets. once you've done this, hand thread in your lag bolt with the bracket free. tighten the bolt down almost all the way then reattach the top of the pull up bar to the support bracket with the supplied bolts. you might have to flex the upper section to align the bolt holes. if you don't do this you'll have to angle the lag bolts in.

I had both my 2 sons on this and myself and it's holding strong. roughly 300lbs. My wife has said the bar is smaller diameter than our current pull up bar. I don't think it'll be an issue. I do like the fact that I can finally do wide pull ups again. Being able to reach out the entire width of the bar is nice. I also like the different angles on the hand holds.

text_fidelity_a:
Suunto 3 Fitness Tracker Sports Watch This is a great fitness watch, but it's not that good of a smart watch. I wouldn't suggest cross shopping this with a Samsung Gear or Apple Watch, as they can do quite a bit more than this. Likewise some of the newer Garmin watches are a bit more capable, but if you're looking for a fitness watch (with some smart watch features), this is a very good option.

It sets up quickly, although the charger is more akin to what I expected from 2015 than 2018. It clips on, and it charges reasonably quickly. It has a guided setup and decent instructions that will help walk you through using the watch. I'd rely on those, as it's not the most intuitive watch. Apple and Samsung have them beat there (I haven't used a Garmin). In regards to use, I find the GPS to be quite accurate (compared to phone) and the heart rate and steps to be accurate (compared to a Fitbit). Both do well compared to my own non-scientific tests (ie the heart rate looked right and the recorded journey matched my recollection).

I would say that a Samsung, Apple (if you use iPhones), and Garmin would be more broadly recommended. This is a bit of a fitness watch for fit people (the Garmin fits the bill there), and it's not a "lifestyle accessory" or gizmo. I found the focus on fitness to be refreshing and a bit of a reminder of what I'm trying to do, but I couldn't send tunes to my earbuds or other stuff I can do with some of my other watches. I find it to be a solid tradeoff, but it may not be for you.

4 stars for being a bit niche but not being absolutely amazing at that niche.
text_fidelity_b: Suunto 3 Fitness Tracker Sports Watch

I predict I'll get another couple years out of it before the battery becomes unreliable for anything more than a run around the neighborhood. I've got an old Forerunner 101 that I bought back in the early 2000s that I prefer over the Fenix. It's comically bulky, but runs on AAA batteries, so you can just keep going and going and going. I wish Garmin would have kept the Forerunner line.

text_fidelity_a: MPOWERD Luci - The Original Inflatable Solar Light, Clear Finish I was laid off in Sept 2013 from a govt contract job. My family has been reduced to living in an RV. We are always looking for ways to reduce our expenses. I found this product by accident. I was at Big 5 buying a diamond knife sharpener. They had these sitting on the check out counter. The price was right at $12.99. I have used and made similar products in the past with mixed results, such as solar yard lights. I bought one. I turned it on when the sunset after charging for about an hour. We have our RV parked behind an abandoned house in the Arizona desert.  It gets real dark, real fast. This little light lit up our whole front yard area. It held the charge for a few hours. Inside the RV it was even better. I bought 3 more the next day! I have one in the bathroom, one in the living room, and two for the bedroom. I charge them by hanging then from our clothes line or one of the mesquite trees. I can get a few nights intermittent use from them on a single day in the sun. They have quickly become a necessary peice of gear for our involuntary reduced life style. When we spend a nice evening outside I place them in the trees and the four lights illuminate the yard better than 4 strands of 100 clear led xmas lights. I will buy more. We have friends in the homeless community and they will be getting these as gifts as funds allow. Waterproof, rugged, renewable. Two things would make them perfect, a USB port for emergency device charging,  and a photocell circut to allow them to charge during the day and come on automatically at night. I'm an Iraq war vet and I wish these were available in 2008. We were always losing power and we never lacked sunshine during the day. Batteries were not always available and being an avid reader due to insomnia, this product would have saved me many a boring night staring into darkness.
text_fidelity_b: MPOWERD Luci - The Original Inflatable Solar Light, Clear Finish

text_fidelity_a: Foxelli Carbon Fiber Trekking Poles – Lightweight Collapsible Hiking Poles, Shock-Absorbent Walking Sticks with Natural Cork Grips, Flip Locks, 4 Season/All Terrain Accessories and Carry Bag First of all, I used to be one of those people who thought trekking poles were for wusses, but as I've gotten a bit older and wiser I have found that they are indispensable for longer hikes. I can hike twice as far with them and they really help with some challenging up and downs. These poles look great and are comfortable to use.  I went on one 10 mile hike when I first used them. I did find that the pole adjustment locks took some getting used to.  You have to turn a knob and then flip the clip to lock it into position. If you tighten the screw too much then there is too much tension and you can't flip the clip, so you have to go back and loosen the screw a bit more and then try again. Once I got the hang of it, it was fairly simple. I would suggest doing it before you leave the house. I'd also suggest leaning hard on each pole to be sure it's locked firmly.  Also, when putting the mud guards on, it helps to screw them on to the threads at the pole bases and then push on firmly. I lost one mudguard (in some really deep mud.) The Foxelli company's customer service is excellent though and they sent a replacement pair out right away!  These come with a nice bag and two sets of tips (one for storage and one for asphalt) and two sets of guards (one for dirt and one for snow.)
text_fidelity_b: Foxelli Carbon Fiber Trekking Poles – Lightweight Collapsible Hiking Poles, Shock-Absorbent Walking Sticks with Natural Cork Grips, Flip Locks, 4 Season/All Terrain Accessories and Carry Bag

Sport-Brella Umbrella Chair - 360 Degree Sun Protection Chair I couldn't wait to try this Sport-Brella Umbrella Chair just for the sun protection alone. I thought, what a great idea, sun coverage any where you go outdoors in an instant! The chair is just like any shoulder carry-type folding chair- easy to open, set up and close. It's comfortable on the seating and arms. It has an arm cup holder and front zip pocket for storage with a bottle opener on the zipper tab. The umbrella opens and closes with ease and you can place it on either side of the chair. You can also adjust the umbrella with a full 360 degree rotation.

It's all great except for one major flaw. The umbrella has this teensy tiny plastic tab that you push into either side of the chair that will hold this umbrella in place. The smallest gust of wind lifts the umbrella up and out of the umbrella holder breaking off this teensy tiny tab leaving you with an umbrella that no longer locks in place, and of course chasing an umbrella wherever the wind decides to take it. This was a perfect idea made so cheaply that it makes the best part- the umbrella- pretty much useless in any wind. The gust of wind that lifted this umbrella out of the holder was actually a light breeze, so I can't imagine what a real gust of strong wind would do to this umbrella. It's such a shame that the company SKLZ didn't put in a few cents more for a stronger metal tab which could have made this chair a real winner instead of a waste of a design which is what it really is. It is still a nice chair that does shade you, but only on a very still day when you have no movement of air, which makes the main part I like- the umbrella pretty useless to me.
text_fidelity_b: Sport-Brella Umbrella Chair - 360 Degree Sun Protection Chair

text_fidelity_a: Rapala Ike's Custom Ink DT (Dives-To) Series Crankbait A little heavier/bigger (fatter) than I was expecting, I might have misread the chart when ordering. Dives deep and quick, lots of action. Runs true. Using a medium-light to medium action rod with 8 lb test it is a bit heavy but the rod tip tells the tale. A constant wiggle, tight but heavy wiggle. Good action. Did not test the depth completely, the one I bought was for a 10ft dive. Ran it in 6 foot of water and kissed the bottom in no time. It gets down fast. Should be a good lure, skips the bottom but doesn`t dig in. Large lip tends to bump off items.
text_fidelity_b: Rapala Ike's Custom Ink DT (Dives-To) Series Crankbait
